comments.body:
Use `Text.from_markup(value).plain` to get the displayed text without the markup. Keep the original string for the menu, and use the plain text only as the search key.

For the `filter_options()` in your linked Beaupy example:

```python
from rich.text import Text

def filter_options(*, options: list[str], substring: str) -> list[str]:
    if not substring:
        return list(options)
    needle = substring.lower()
    return [
        item
        for item in options
        if needle in Text.from_markup(item).plain.lower()
    ]
```

For example, `[bold red]Apple[/bold red]` is searched as `Apple`: `red` no longer matches, while `app` does. The returned item still contains its original styling.

I checked this search function with Rich 15.0.0, including style-name exclusion, case-insensitive visible text, link text versus its hidden URL, empty filters, emoji expansion, and escaped literal brackets. This checks the filtering step, not a complete interactive Beaupy session.

[API reference](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/text.html#rich.text.Text.from_markup)

AI assistance disclosure: prepared and tested for Youngseok Oh using OpenAI Codex.
